note: E17-L02's definitions: the Neon League's two lane conditions and its kit. The three Neon boss rules (Oil Slick, Narrow Lane, Strobe) were written in E17-D03 and E17-D05. E18-C13 (the rules of E17-L02) landed Long Oil and Two-Tone; the Neon Kit stays here until E22-L02 makes the League live.

item.name: Neon Kit
item.downside: No Hammer or Echo Ball: six cards split between curve and straight, with no power or retrigger ball.

design.trigger: Start a Neon League attempt with ten Wood pins, a deck of three Hook Balls and three Spare Balls (the House Ball is always available) and $6.
design.pool: Starting kit: chosen on the League Board for the Neon League; available from the start, as the League is.
design.presentation_needs: A kit card in Neon colours with a curve and a straight line crossing; the binder shows its loadout.

design.trigger: The oil runs to 47 ft (14.33 m) instead of the standard 40 ft (12.19 m), so a charged spin has less dry backend to hook in: the same charge curves later and less. Straight throws are unaffected, and the backend's friction is unchanged.
design.pool: Lane condition: never in a shop; listed in a League's lane pool (Neon League spec).
design.presentation_needs: A glowing line where the oil ends, further down the lane than on House Oil, readable from the behind-ball view without colour; the HUD and the shop's next-match preview name it; the aim preview reflects the later hook.

design.trigger: On the left half of the lane (the bowler's left of the centre board) the oil ends at 34 ft (10.36 m) instead of 40 ft, so a ball rolling there reaches the dry backend sooner and a charged spin hooks earlier and further. The right half keeps the standard pattern. Straight throws are unaffected.
design.pool: Lane condition: never in a shop; listed in a League's lane pool (Neon League spec).
design.presentation_needs: Two clearly different halves (a pattern or texture split down the centre board, not colour alone), each glowing to where its oil ends; the HUD and the next-match preview name it; the aim preview reflects which half the ball travels on.
